battle.name: 唐諸王反武后之戰
battle.brief: 垂拱四年（688）九月，豫州刺史李沖舉兵反武則天，號匡復唐室，據本州城與鄰縣而鬥，不到一月為官軍所平，李沖出奔被擒，押送洛陽就誅。叛眾多為臨時聚集的鄉人，器械不備，官軍以數州之兵會剿並斷其糧道。卡面秦連弩正屬守城壓制攻城者的器械，城頭弩列是把登城之敵釘在牆外的關鍵。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰的一方是武周朝廷，即以女皇武則天為核心、駐洛陽的中央政府。高宗崩後，武則天自684年以皇太后身分臨朝稱制，690年進號聖神皇帝，正式稱帝；其下有尚書省、門下省、侍中與御史台，首都宿衛為羽林軍與萬騎，州府設刺史與兵曹參軍，邊軍則早已改為募兵編制，府兵舊制僅存於名號。叛方是唐宗室旁支與地方官員拼成的聯軍，以匡復唐室為號，名義上擁護高宗與中宗一脈的正統，實際上由起事的宗室王公自行節制，因起事倉促，並無統一軍令、編制與糧秣。值得留意的是，朝廷在平亂前夕起用一批宗室與武氏姻親出任要州刺史，本意是分權防範，結果反而令握有地方兵柄的刺史同時握有舉兵問鼎的資源。戰端一開，州兵、團結與臨時募集的鄉勇成了作戰主力，中央禁軍只作最後的鎮壓與掃尾。雙方的指揮體系都是以行政官員兼領軍事，缺少獨立的野戰統帥制度，這一點直接決定了戰事的節奏。
countriesEn: One side was the court of the Wu Zhou, that is, the central government seated at Luoyang under the Empress Wu Zetian. After Gaozong died, Wu Zetian had ruled as empress dowager and regent from 684, and in 690 she took the title of the Sage and Divine Emperor and became emperor in her own right. Under her stood the Department of State Affairs, the Chancellery, the Secretariat and the Censorate; the guard of the capital was the Feathered Guard and the Flying Cavalry; the prefectures had a cishi and a bingcao with a military adjutant; and the frontier armies had long since been converted to recruited troops, with the old fubing system surviving only as a name. The other side was a coalition patched together from collateral branches of the Tang imperial clan and from local officials. It marched under the banner of restoring the Tang house, claimed in theory to uphold the legitimate line of Gaozong and Zhongzong, and in fact was directed by the princely rebels themselves; because the rising was launched in haste, it had no unified command, no establishment and no supply. It is worth noticing that shortly before the rising was put down, the court had put a batch of princes of the clan and kinsmen of the Wu family in charge of the key prefectures, meaning to divide authority and forestall exactly this kind of danger. The result was that the men who held the troops of a province also held the resources for raising an army. Once fighting began, the provincial militia, the local levy and villagers enrolled in haste formed the bulk of the combatants, while the central guard was used only for the last work of suppression and mopping up. On both sides the chain of command was simply administrative office combined with military command, and neither had an independent system of field command; that fact alone set the tempo of the whole affair.
people: 核心人物是起兵的宗室諸王與平叛的朝廷將領。宗室方面，記錄最詳的是豫州刺史李沖，其父為武則天之兄、宗室王李元慶，李沖以王公身分出守外州，垂拱四年九月舉兵，旋即敗亡，事後被押送洛陽誅死。同一時期汝州一線還有越王李貞、譚王李元嘉等同族起事與被誅的記載，李貞兵敗服毒自盡，這一組事繫於哪一年，諸說並存，有繫於684年者，也有繫於687至688年者。平叛一方，朝廷派出的統帥多不見於傳世記載，只留下行軍總管、刺史這類名號；較可確認的是內史與兵部尚書一級的中央官員奉詔督軍，地方上則由鄰州刺史率兵會剿。武則天本人是這場衝突真正的對手與推手：她在684年廢中宗、立睿宗而臨朝，686年設銅匭讓臣民投書，687至688年間加建明堂、籌議封禪。宗室對她的清算意圖，與她對宗室的清洗互相推高。私家筆記與編年史對起事者的家世記數互有出入，多數記載強調李沖素來驕矜、不習兵事，其眾多為市井之民；至於起事者究竟有多少可戰之兵、各州響應者幾家，則無一字可考，諸說並存。
peopleEn: The central figures were the Tang princes who rose and the commanders the court sent against them. On the rebel side the best documented is Li Chong, governor of Yu prefecture, whose father was Li Yuanqing, a prince of the clan and brother of Wu Zetian. Holding the rank of a princely kinsman, Li Chong had been posted to a frontier prefecture, and in the ninth month of the fourth year of Chuigong he raised troops, was defeated almost at once, and was afterwards escorted to Luoyang and put to death. From the same period there are also records, partly at variance with one another, of other members of the clan rising and being executed in the line of Ru prefecture, among them the Prince of Yue Li Zhen and the Prince of Tan Li Yuanjia; Li Zhen was defeated and took poison to his own death. To which year this group of events belongs is given variously: some place them in 684, others in 687 or 688. On the side of the suppression, the names of the leaders the court dispatched are largely absent from the transmitted records, leaving only such formulas as the commander of the marching army or the prefect; what can be confirmed is that officials of the rank of the Senior Secretary and of the minister of war were sent with imperial commissions to supervise the campaign, and that prefects of the neighbouring provinces led their own troops in to join in. Wu Zetian herself was the true opponent and the driving force behind this conflict. In 684 she deposed Zhongzong, enthroned Ruizong and ruled as regent; in 686 she set up the bronze box for the remonstrance of the people; and between 687 and 688 she pushed ahead with the building of the Hall of Light and the planning of the Fengshan sacrifice. The intent to purge the clan and the clan's own fear of being purged pushed each other higher. Private notes and the chronological histories differ on the birth and the doings of the rebels, and most of the accounts stress that Li Chong had always been proud and had never learned the art of war, and that his followers were largely ordinary townsmen. As for how many fighting men the rebels really had and how many prefectures answered them, not a single word of the record settles it, and the views differ.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩在這場戰役裡的位置，是守城壓制，而不是野戰廳殺。它的機括把弩弦的拉力先行儲存，上弦之後踩動板機即可連發，射手在城頭不必反覆上弦，專門用來射擊攀城的敵兵，以及推動雲梯、衝車的攻方。秦弩機的形制在漢代已經成熟，馬鈞、諸葛亮一系又把連發之數推得更高，但兵書記載中它長期是守城、水戰與隘口防守的器械，唐代州城與關塞的城頭同樣配置強弩、擲車與飛樓，弩手有上柱、下柱之別。叛軍則完全沒有這類器械，其眾多為臨時聚集的鄉人，器械不備，主要靠弓、刀、槊、長矛與簡單的雲梯攻城，攻城器械靠臨時徵集與破壞所得。防護上，朝廷禁軍有明光甲、彩飾的儀仗甲與馬鎧，州府守軍則以皮甲、札甲為主，長槊與陌刀並列。補給與運力方面，武周的租庸調與和糴制度仍在運作，洛陽的糧秣可由汴渠、洛水與驛道調撥，而豫州、陳州一線的州縣倉儲與漕運，恰好決定了起事能撐多久。由此可以看出，為何以連弩守城的軍隊能把烏合之眾釘在城外，而叛軍首先敗在糧秣與攻具，不是敗在戰陣的勝負。
kitsEn: The place of the Qin repeating crossbow on the card in this campaign is on the side of defence, holding the attacker down, and not on that of the open-field killing. Its mechanism stores the strain of the bowstring in advance, so that once the bow is drawn the soldier can release shot after shot by pressing a treadle, and the archer on the wall need not go back to the winding of the string; it exists to shoot at the men climbing the wall and at the crews pushing scaling ladders and battering rams. The form of the Qin trigger mechanism had already matured by the Han, and the line of Ma Jun and Zhuge Liang raised the number of bolts fired from a single loading still further, yet in the military manuals it remained for a long while an instrument of the defence of walled towns, of river fighting and of passes. The strong crossbows, the throwing engines and the flying towers of the Tang city walls and frontier forts were organised in the same way, the crossbowmen being divided into the upper pillar and the lower pillar. The rebels had no such instruments at all. Their followers were villagers gathered together at the last moment, short of equipment, and they relied on bows, knives, spears, long pikes and simple scaling ladders, their siege gear being whatever they could take from local households or tear down. On the side of protection, the central guard had bright armour, gilt and coloured ceremonial harness and horse armour, while the provincial garrisons were furnished mainly with leather and lamellar armour, with long pikes and the pole sword side by side. As for supply and transport, the rent, labour and corvee system of the Wu Zhou was still in operation, the grain of Luoyang could be shifted by the Bian canal, the Luo river and the post roads, and the granaries and the water traffic of the prefectures of Yu and Chen decided exactly how long the rising could last. All this explains why a garrison armed with the repeating crossbow could pin a mob outside the walls, and why the rebel side failed first on supplies and siege gear rather than on the field of battle.
tactics: 叛軍的戰法可用一句話概括：靠人數與地利硬推，不靠編制。李沖起兵於豫州，既未先取洛陽，也沒有南聯揚州舊例之師，更沒有與契丹、吐蕃取得配合；他選擇的是據守本州治所、向外掃掠郡縣的方略，試圖用攻掠補給拖住官軍。起事初期兵鋒直指鄰縣與驛道，但因缺乏攻城技術與遠程火力，遇到有城郭與弩手防守的縣城便久攻不下。官軍的應對則循唐廷平叛的常例：由中央遣使持節發兵，附近各州兵會剿，同時守住驛道與漕運，切斷叛軍的糧源；圍城不急攻，多用長圍與斷糧迫其自潰，捕獲首惡後再分兵搜捕餘黨。城防一端，守軍憑城頭弩列與連弩持續射擊，壓住接近的雲梯，並在城下列陣衝擊那些反覆試圖登城的隊伍。李沖本人不習兵事，軍紀與號令混亂，部眾在不利於己的野外交戰與斷糧壓力下迅速瓦解。戰事前後不足一月即告結束，唐廷隨即在豫、陳二州更換刺史、改易州名，並把宗室中有兵柄者調離要地。
tacticsEn: The method of the rebels can be put in a single phrase: they pushed forward on the strength of numbers and of local advantage, and not on the strength of organisation. Li Chong rose in Yu prefecture; he did not strike at Luoyang first, did not link up with the old model of the Yangzhou rising, and had no coordination with the Khitan or with Tibet. What he chose was to hold the seat of his own prefecture and sweep out into the neighbouring commanderies, trying to sustain himself on what he could plunder and to hold the government troops at bay. The first thrust of the rising was directed at the neighbouring counties and at the post road, but for want of siegecraft and of long-range fire, once a county town with walls and crossbowmen was encountered the siege dragged on. The court's answer followed the usual Tang procedure for putting down a rising: the centre sent commissioners with imperial commissions to raise troops, the prefectures of the neighbouring provinces joined in the attack, and at the same time the post road and the grain traffic were held, cutting the rebels off from their supplies. Towns were invested rather than stormed, the usual method being to encircle them at distance and cut the grain until they gave themselves up; once the principal culprits were taken, the remaining bands were hunted down county by county. On the side of the defence, the garrison shot from the ranks of crossbows and from the repeating crossbows on the wall, keeping the scaling ladders at a distance, and formed up below the walls to strike again and again at the columns that tried to mount. Li Chong himself had never learned the art of war, the discipline and the call-signs of his force were in confusion, and his ranks dissolved quickly under the weight of unfavourable field conditions and of the pressure of hunger. The whole affair was over in less than a month, after which the Tang court replaced the prefects of Yu and Chen, changed the names of the prefectures, and transferred out of the key posts the members of the imperial clan who held troops.
data: 可核對的數字不多，需分開看。第一類是年表：起事繫於垂拱四年（688）九月，另有諸書繫於垂拱三年（687）九月，諸說並存；武則天自684年臨朝、690年稱帝，至705年退位，在位二十餘年；銅匭設於686年，銅匭、推事院與告密之制構成本案的制度背景；明堂之建始於688年，歷時數年而成；705年神龍政變後中宗復位，是唐諸王反武則天這一輪反亂的最終結局。第二類是編制與地名：平叛主力為數州之兵與臨時募兵，禁軍只用於收尾，其具體人數各書不載；起事在豫州（治今河南汝州）與鄰近的陳州（今河南淮陽）一帶，洛陽是朝廷的徵發與指揮中心，驛道與汴渠、洛水構成本區的補給線。第三類是需要打折的推估：叛軍規模諸書概以烏合之眾形容，無任何具體人數記載；官軍人數同樣沒有可靠數字。史書常說叛軍素不習兵、器械不備、旬月而平，此類定性描述的可信度高於任何具體人數。關於本戰役的兵員損耗，傳世諸史均未留下可核之數，本篇亦不作推算。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are few, and they have to be taken apart. The first class is the chronology. The rising is tied to the ninth month of the fourth year of Chuigong (688), though some books tie it to the ninth month of the third year (687), and the views differ. Wu Zetian ruled as regent from 684 and as emperor from 690 until her own deposition in 705, a span of more than twenty years. The bronze box for remonstrance was set up in 686; the bronze box, the Court of Remonstrance and the system of informers together form the institutional background of this case. Work on the Hall of Light began in 688 and took several years to finish. The coup of 705, after which Zhongzong was restored, was the final settlement of this round of rising by the princes against Empress Wu. The second class is establishments and place names. The main body of the army that suppressed the rising was made up of the troops of several prefectures together with hastily enrolled levies, the central guard being used only to finish the job, and the numbers are nowhere recorded. The rising took place in Yu prefecture, whose seat was at what is now Ruzhou in Henan, and in the neighbouring Chen prefecture, at what is now Huaiyang in Henan. Luoyang was the centre from which the court levied and directed everything, and the post road together with the Bian canal and the Luo river formed the supply line of this region. The third class is estimate, and must be discounted. The size of the rebel force is generally described in the histories as a mob of townsmen, with no figure of any kind given; the number of the government troops is equally without a reliable figure. The histories commonly say that the rebels had never been trained, were short of equipment, and were crushed within a month; such qualitative statements are far more trustworthy than any specific number. As for the losses in men, the transmitted histories leave nothing that can be checked, and this account does not estimate them.
cause: 起事的原因有多層，最近的一層是權力安排。武則天以藩邸舊人與宗室姻親出任要州刺史，濃縮了地方兵柄，宗室王公以為這是要把唐室的江山一寸寸換成武氏的；686年銅匭、推事院與酷吏告密同時並行，朝廷對宗室的不信任公開化，宗室人人自危，這是唐諸王反武則天得以成事的土壤。往上一層是繼承合法性：684年高宗崩，中宗即位兩月被廢，睿宗復居東宮而無所事事，武則天以皇太后臨朝稱制，宗室名正言順地以高宗所立自居，認為國本被篡。往下一層是財政與徭役：明堂、封禪、銅匭與各種營造同時舉行，州縣被抽調的丁役與轉運年年增加，民間對朝廷的怨望，轉成地方刺史可以順勢利用的號召力。最後是戰略層面：唐廷在關內與中原的宿衛與州兵系統仍然完整，起事者清楚知道必須速戰速決、先取本州、以攻養戰，否則一旦被合圍斷糧，烏合之眾必然瓦解。諸說並存的是：究竟是李沖等人先有匡復之志而後擇時，還是武則天逼人太甚、逼出反者；史無一字可據其動機，此點只能存疑。
causeEn: There were several layers behind the rising, and the nearest one concerns the arrangement of power. Wu Zetian put her own household followers and kinsmen of the imperial clan in charge of the key prefectures, concentrating the military authority of the provinces, and the princes of the clan took it to mean that the Tang realm was being handed over to the Wu family by the inch. In 686 the bronze box, the Court of Remonstrance and the campaign of the informers went forward together; the open distrust of the court towards the clan made every prince feel that his life was in danger, and that was the soil in which a rising by the princes against Empress Wu could take root. One layer further up lies the legitimacy of succession. Gaozong died in 684; Zhongzong was enthroned and deposed within two months; Ruizong was put back in the eastern palace with nothing to do; Wu Zetian ruled as empress dowager and regent; and the clan on the strength of its own title claimed to represent what Gaozong had established, holding that the foundation of the state had been usurped. One layer further down lies the fiscal and corvee pressure. The Hall of Light, the Fengshan sacrifice, the bronze box and the various building programmes all went forward at once, the localities were drained of labour and of transport year after year, and the resentment of the countryside was turned by the provincial governors into a slogan they could exploit. Finally there is the strategic layer. The system of the capital guard and of the provincial troops in the Guanzhong and in the Central Plain was still intact, and the rebels knew perfectly well that they had to fight quickly, seize their own prefecture first and sustain themselves on what they took; otherwise, once they were surrounded and their grain cut, a mob of this kind was bound to come apart. What remains disputed is this: whether Li Chong and his fellows first had the intention of restoring the house and afterwards chose their moment, or whether Wu Zetian's pressure was so great that the rebels were driven out. Not a single word of the record allows their motive to be settled, and the point must be left open.
impact: 平叛之後，武周對宗室的防範反而收得更緊：豫、陳一帶的刺史被撤換，州名被改，兵柄更集中到武氏與近幸手中，宗室此後再沒有一次成形的武力起義，直到705年由宰相與禁軍以政變方式完成復唐。這是唐諸王反武則天最重要的一項後果——宗室的槍杆子被削掉，復唐只能靠政變而非內戰。反過來看，這種削枝也留下隱患：地方上同時出現國兵不屬於國家的苗頭，州兵、募兵與宿衛各聽其主，中央每一次清洗都讓武將更獨立，節度使的割據正是在此後二三十年裡逐步長出來的，可以視為唐中期格局的一條遠因。制度層面上，銅匭、告密與酷吏政治雖在697年後逐步收束，但本案證明了一件事：以告密維持的統治，把宗室與官僚系統推向同一個方向，各自尋找讓對方無法再起兵的辦法。技術層面上，弩與連弩在州城防務中的地位再次被確認，攻守兩端都圍繞能不能把兵壓在牆外這個問題展開，這條經驗一直延續到宋代城防的弩手編制。歷史記載方面，關於此役的分歧多集中在兩點：起事的確切年月，以及李沖眾人的數目，二者諸說並存，學者多採垂拱四年、眾無定數的說法。
impactEn: After the rising was put down, the Wu court's guard against the imperial clan was drawn tighter rather than relaxed. The prefects of the Yu and Chen areas were replaced, the names of the prefectures were changed, and military authority was concentrated further into the hands of the Wu family and their favourites. From then on the clan of Tang never mounted another armed rising of its own, and until 705 the restoration of the house was carried out by a coup of the chancellors and of the guard rather than by civil war. That is the most important consequence of the war of the Tang princes against Empress Wu: the clan's arms were cut away, and the restoration could only be achieved by a palace coup instead of by a rebellion. Read the other way, this pruning of the branches left a hidden danger. At the same time the first signs appeared of troops that did not belong to the state, for the provincial militia, the recruited soldiers and the palace guard each answered to their own masters, and every purge at the centre left the generals more independent of it. The power of the regional military governors grew out of that in the two or three decades that followed, and this can be taken as one of the remote causes of the situation in the middle Tang. At the institutional level, the bronze box, the informers and the policy of the harsh officials were wound back step by step after 697, but this case proves one thing: a rule maintained by informing turns the imperial clan and the official class in the same direction, each looking for a way to make the other unable to raise an army again. At the technical level, the standing of the crossbow and of the repeating crossbow in the defence of walled towns was confirmed once more, for the assaulting side and the defending side alike turned on a single question, whether the enemy could be kept out beyond the wall; that experience runs on into the organisation of the crossbowmen in the walled defences of the Song. In the historical record, the disputes about this campaign cluster on two points, the exact year and month of the rising and the number of Li Chong's men; both are given variously, and the usual scholarly choice is the fourth year of Chuigong with no fixed number.
result: 結果很簡單：叛軍被平，李沖被誅，唐諸王反武則天的一輪武裝嘗試以失敗告終。起事自豫州爆發，至其被平不出一月，朝廷由中央發兵、鄰州會剿、斷糧圍剿三路並進，迅速拆散了那批臨時聚集的鄉兵，首惡押送洛陽處斬，餘黨分州捕治，州刺史一律更替，州名亦因之改易。這一役之後，武則天對宗室的清洗與對地方的控制同時加固，明堂仍照原計興建，銅匭照舊懸於朝堂，直到690年她正式稱帝，690至705年間再沒有宗室武力反叛。也正因如此，705年神龍元年張柬之、崔玄暐、敬暉、桓彥範、袁恕己、張暠與太平公主等以禁軍政變的方式迫中宗復位時，能夠打的牌並不是兵馬，而是正統的名分與廢立之權——宗室用了十五年時間失去槍杆子，最後靠一次宮門之變拿回皇位。這正是唐諸王反武則天之戰留下的全部教訓。
resultEn: The outcome was simple. The rebels were crushed, Li Chong was executed, and the round of armed attempt by the Tang princes against Empress Wu ended in failure. The rising began in Yu prefecture, and it was over in less than a month. The court moved on three fronts at once, sending out troops from the centre, drawing in the troops of the neighbouring prefectures and cutting the grain road, and it broke up within a short time that mass of villagers gathered together at the last moment. The principal culprits were escorted to Luoyang and beheaded, the remaining bands were hunted down and dealt with in each prefecture, the governors were replaced throughout, and the names of the prefectures were changed in consequence. After this campaign the purge of the clan and the control of the localities were both tightened: the Hall of Light went on being built as planned, the bronze box still hung in the court, and from 690, when she took the imperial title in earnest, no prince of the clan rose in arms again before 705. Precisely for this reason, when in the first year of Shenlong, 705, Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, Yuan Shuji, Zhang Gao and Princess Taiping used the guard to stage a coup and compelled Zhongzong to take the throne again, the card they could play was not troops but the legitimacy of the orthodox line and the right to depose and enthrone. The princes of the Tang had spent fifteen years losing their arms, and at the end they took back the throne with a single stroke at the palace gate. That is the whole lesson left by the war of the Tang princes against Empress Wu.
